transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Martinez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CardioAI CTO), Raj Patel (ML Infra), Marta Silva (Product)

Summary:
Short demo of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles and console walkthrough. Focus on INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs for CardioAI's clinical summarization model; baseline latency and fidelity expectations; pilot next steps and security questions.

Topics covered:
- Quick baseline numbers (p50/p95 latency) for INT8 and FP8 on rtx-like hosts (approx)
- Quality regressions: hallucination metrics, rouge/answer accuracy on medical prompts
- Batching, KV cache impacts, and dynamic quantization behavior
- Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC concerns for CardioAI
- Sandbox and pilot scope

Action items (in-meeting):
- Ethan to run A/B with customer prompts; export latency/quality deltas
- Maya to share pricing tiers and security docs
- Raj to provide sample corpus and sequence length stats

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, account owner for CardioAI. Quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: Hi, Lena Ortiz. CTO at CardioAI. We're looking to reduce per-call cost and keep latency under 300ms for our summarization endpoint.
[00:15] Raj: Raj Patel, infra. We run inference on hybrid cloud, some on-prem for PHI. Interested in quant profiles and private deploy options.
[00:22] Marta: Marta Silva, product, happy to be here.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Ethan, want to kick off with the Optimize console?
[00:28] Ethan: Sure. I'll share my screen now. Give me a sec. Ok, heading into Optimize, the quant profiles page. Note - we precomputed INT8 and FP8 profiles for the common open-clinical models but we'll show how to upload your own eval set too.
[01:02] Ethan: So first slide — baseline. On a T4-class host we saw p50 token latency at around 12ms for FP8 and 9ms for INT8 for short sequences, but that delta flips for longer seqs because FP8 preserves more numeric headroom. For whole request p95 numbers we typically see FP8 p95 ~ 210ms vs INT8 p95 ~ 170ms for 512-token summaries, with quality delta of approximate 1.8% measured on our internal rouge-like metric.
[01:45] Raj: Those numbers are helpful. Our target is p95 < 300ms so both look fine, but the quality hit is the concern. How are you measuring quality?
[01:53] Ethan: Good question. We run a paired A/B on your prompt set and measure a combination of exact match on structured fields, a domain-aware rouge, and hallucination rate scored by annotators. For CardioAI we recommend keeping a small holdout of high-sensitivity prompts and asserting no more than 1% increase in hallucination.
[02:20] Lena: Can you show the console where we compare the two profiles side by side?
[02:24] Ethan: Yep. Here - the console lets you import your sample set, pick INT8 and FP8 candidate profiles, and run batch eval. The UI shows token-level breakdown, latency histogram, and a quality delta heatmap.
[02:40] Ethan: small caveat to note: quantization sensitivity varies by layer and by activation distribution. For some clinical models we've seen certain heads being super sensitive, and that yields jumps in hallucination even with small loss in average rouge. The Optimize tool surfaces suspect prompts.
[03:10] Marta: Nice. If a prompt is flagged, can we exclude it from production or route it to FP8?
[03:16] Ethan: Exactly. You can create routing policies - route by prompt tag, by customer tier, or by latency budget. So critical prompts can hit FP8 while bulk can go to INT8. That gives cost savings without exposing sensitive outputs.
[03:34] Lena: About private deployment: we need KMS integration and audit logs. Is that supported?
[03:39] Maya: Yes, Private and Dedicated both support KMS/HSM in customer VPCs and we stream audit logs to your SIEM. We'll attach the SOC 2 and security deck after.
[03:48] Raj: For on-prem, do you support air-gapped package? We have PHI in some tenants.
[03:52] Ethan: We do. The private package can be deployed in air-gapped mode. There are some kernel-level optimizations that we compile into the runtime; we provide signed binaries and an install playbook.
[04:05] Lena: Could you walk through a concrete example with our 1k prompt set?
[04:09] Ethan: Absolutely. So imagine we run both INT8 and FP8 against your 1k prompts. The console will produce a report: average latency, tail latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k requests, and quality deltas for defined metrics. We'll show a scatter plot of latency vs quality, you can pick an operating point.
[04:33] Ethan: Example numbers from a similar customer: INT8 reduced token cost by ~28% and improved throughput but had a 2.1% degradation on domain-specific entity extraction. For them we did a hybrid rollout - 80% INT8, 20% FP8 for entity-critical routes.
[04:55] Raj: How easy is rollback if we see regressions in production?
[05:00] Ethan: You can configure automatic fallback policies. If a monitored metric crosses a threshold, traffic shifts back to the safe profile. Rollouts support canary windows and A/B.
[05:12] Marta: What about batching? We often batch client requests to amortize overhead. Does INT8/FP8 behavior change under batching?
[05:20] Ethan: Under batching, kernel selection changes and you generally see better throughput efficiency; but latency SLOs depend on queueing thresholds. INT8's smaller compute can benefit more from larger batches. Optimize suggests batch size per profile given your SLOs.
[05:40] Maya: Quick note on cost math - the console shows estimated cost per 1M tokens for each profile and also factors in cache hit rates.
[05:48] Lena: You mentioned KV cache. We're heavy on conversational contexts, so cache hit rate is high. How does cache change the decision?
[05:56] Ethan: If KV cache reuse is high, per-token compute drops and quantization impact is less in cost terms. But quality still needs to be checked because cached tokens bypass some recomputation. The console models prefix caching and shows effective cost per logical token.
[06:15] Raj: Any approximate numbers on memory/footprint for INT8 vs FP8? We're GPU constrained.
[06:20] Ethan: Roughly INT8 halves memory for activations in many paths vs FP16; FP8 sits between INT8 and FP16 depending on format. But quantization schemes differ by layer and your actual memory delta depends on how much we quantize (weights-only vs weights+activations). The Optimize recommendations include memory profiles per hardware type.
[06:45] Lena: For the pilot, we want to measure quality on a handful of clinically sensitive prompts - if we pass, expand.
[06:53] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll set up an A/B with those prompts held out and produce a failing prompt list if any prompt exceeds your hallucination budget.
[07:04] Maya: I'm going to demo the export report now. You'll see columns: prompt id, seq length, gold answers, pred_fp8, pred_int8, rouge_delta, hallucination_flag, lat_fp8, lat_int8.
[07:23] Ethan: There's a neat feature - per-prompt confidence delta. It flags when the model's internal scoring shifts. That was helpful for another health customer to find subtle degradations.
[07:33] Raj: On infra side, can we run the benchmark in our VPC? We prefer not to upload samples externally.
[07:39] Ethan: Yes. We can spin a sandbox in your VPC or provide a self-hosted runner that uploads only the aggregated metrics. The console supports both.
[07:51] Lena: Good. How do we interpret the quality delta numbers? What's acceptable?
[07:55] Ethan: We'll propose thresholds based on your SLOs. For example, for entity extraction maybe max 1% absolute drop. For free-form summarization you might accept 0.5-1.5 point rouge drop depending on downstream impact.
[08:10] Marta: Is there tooling to automatically create the routing rules? We have 15 different prompt categories.
[08:15] Ethan: You can create rule templates and apply them by tag. There's also an API so your infra can dynamically tag requests.
[08:25] Maya: Let's talk pricing briefly. We have per-token hosted pricing and dedicated capacity. For pilots most customers start hosted, then move to dedicated once throughput needs justify the reserved pool.
[08:38] Lena: For dedicated, do you guarantee latency SLOs?
[08:42] Maya: Yes, dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput and lower p95 targets; exact numbers are in the pricing doc we'll send.
[08:49] Raj: A couple technical nitty-gritty things - does the runtime support fused attention kernels and what about fp8 kernel stability across GPU driver versions?
[08:58] Ethan: We select kernels per hardware and have compatibility tests. For FP8 we lock CUDA and driver versions in private installs; the hosted service manages that for you. We also provide a matrix of supported driver versions.
[09:12] Lena: Let's do a quick live example. Ethan, can you import a short hand-picked set?
[09:16] Ethan: Importing now - I uploaded 20 representative prompts (anonymized). Kicking off eval: running INT8 profile first. This will take a minute.
[09:37] Ethan: Ok INT8 run finished. p50 120ms, p95 185ms on our sandbox instance with batch size 8. FP8 run complete: p50 135ms, p95 205ms. Quality: average rouge-ish metric delta was -1.2% for INT8, -0.4% for FP8. Two prompts flagged for hallucination increase under INT8.
[10:05] Marta: Can we see which prompts were flagged?
[10:08] Ethan: Showing the flagged list now. Prompt 7 and 12 had entity omissions and invented values in INT8. We can click each to see diff between outputs.
[10:20] Lena: That helps. For these two prompts, could we route them to FP8 or to a safety reranker?
[10:27] Ethan: Both are possible. You can also set per-prompt thresholds for the reranker to trigger a stricter penalty. We have a built-in lightweight reranker you can enable.
[10:40] Raj: On the reranker, what's compute overhead?
[10:43] Ethan: It's small - usually 5-12% extra compute depending on model size and reranker complexity.
[10:49] Maya: One more thing on rollouts - you can do progressive increments and the console will plot the metric drift in real time.
[10:58] Lena: This is helpful. Next, security and audit — can you send the exact list of logs and retention?
[11:03] Maya: I'll include the audit log schema and retention options in the security deck.
[11:08] Raj: Great. A couple more questions: if we see minor regressions on edge cases, can we pin model weights while experimenting with quant profiles?
[11:15] Ethan: Yes, you can pin model versions and create quantized variants at the same version. That way weight updates are separate from quant profile rollouts.
[11:26] Lena: What's the typical delta in GPU utilization between INT8 and FP8?
[11:29] Ethan: Typically INT8 yields lower utilization for matrix ops but higher memory bound patterns can flip the correlation. Our Optimize console shows GPU util and recommends instance families.
[11:40] Marta: Onboarding effort — how long until we can run the first A/B?
[11:44] Maya: If you provide the sample set this week, we can have a baseline report within 5 business days.
[11:49] Lena: That timeline works.
[11:51] Ethan: Any blockers for the pilot?
[11:54] Raj: Only that we'll need the sandbox in our VPC for the first run.
[11:58] Ethan: Noted. We'll provision a VPC sandbox and provide a runner.
[12:03] Maya: Okay quick recap and next steps: Ethan will run the A/B and send results, Maya will share pricing and security docs, Raj will provide the 1k prompts and seq length stats. We'll set pilot kickoff after we review the benchmark.
[12:20] Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:24] Maya: Thanks all.

End of transcript
